title: 4 days Lower Upper program review (part. 2)
summary: NH finishes reviewing the calisthenics athlete's lower/upper program, covering both upper days and the second lower day. He cuts 4x10 strength work, keeps one style per slot, builds time-saving supersets of ring and band work, superset abs with deadlift variations, and says a fifth day should be an arm-focused full body day only if needed.
claims: Volume without a progression drive in the rep scheme leaves gains on the table; 4x10 for strength work should be avoided like the plague
4x10 is fine for later accessory sets
Floor press and bench press train different qualities and shouldn't rotate in the same slot; put them on separate days
He does back squats and box front squats on separate days; the box front squat is his only knee flexion that day before hammering the posterior chain
The floor press shortens range unless your leverages are good, making it more triceps-specific
With only two horizontal press days a week on upper/lower, stick to the deep bench press
Rotating pull-up grips is good for elbow and shoulder tendon health since the arms give out before the back under heavy vertical pulling
Presses need lots of volume, and two overhead press days rarely overtax recovery
The overhead press progresses slowly, slower only than curls; feed it a mix of intensity and volume, one heavy day and one volume day
For calisthenics he prefers AMRAP sets without counting reps since you recover to baseline quickly
Timed holds build grip strength and calisthenic skill
Supersets must save time: no rest between exercises and group exercises that use the same equipment, like rings
Giant set of ring dips, elevated pike push-ups and ring support holds for 3-4 sets
Superset banded face pulls with banded curls, adapting angles to one band anchor
Upper day restructure: bench strength, weighted chins, overhead press, then two supersets and go home
The long head of the triceps looked neglected in the program
He loves front squats but doesn't think they're a good time investment for most because they're so technical
Sumo and conventional deficit deadlifts shouldn't rotate in the same slot; pick one style
Lifters think block or rack pulls are fine with a tired lower back, yet they round as soon as they initiate
Deficit pulls work the posterior chain and quads deeper while block pulls work the upper back more; rotate them across days if pairing them is too much
Don't let a lift appear only every 15 days unless a close variation covers it
Most people's thoracic strength gives out on front squats before their legs
4x10 front squats are acceptable since you can reset the rack between sets; he always does 5 reps on front squats
3x8 is excellent for deficit deadlifts and block pulls; evolving rep ranges would be better
Superset deficit deadlifts with L-sits and block pulls with toes-to-bar to train both flexion and contraction of the abs; it improves bracing
Spinal decompression is best done at the end of the workout when warm, not cold before deadlifts
Intense supersets can replace cardio without hurting strength output
Lower days should have the most tonnage but take the least time
Close-grip bench is a deeper ROM than regular bench; try 4x6-10 for progression
Keep ring rows and band work in high rep ranges
Programmers tend to be greedy and add useless movements where neither mind nor body is in it anymore
Traps and perhaps forearms are the only areas lacking; add wrist curls later if wanted
Forget hypertrophy and strength blocks; run the program 7-8 months and keep eating
Stay at four days; tonnage pyramids up toward the end of the week
A fifth day, if wanted, should be an arm day disguised as full body; bigger arms long-term need a dedicated day
exercises: preferred over floor press with 2 press days
needs mix of intensity and volume
Ring dips + pike push-ups + ring support hold
